organizations.description:
Address: 753 NW Fort Sill Blvd. Phone: 580.357.6900 ext 2311 

 The McKinney-Vento program is a federally mandated initiative designed to remove educational barriers for children and youth experiencing unstable or transitionary housing. Under this program, students who lack a fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime residence—including those living in shelters, motels, cars, or "doubled up" with other families due to economic hardship—have the right to immediate school enrollment, even if they lack typical required paperwork like birth certificates or immunization records. The program works to ensure these students receive equal access to the same free, appropriate public education as their peers, providing support such as school enrollment assistance, school of origin stability, school transportation assistance, and connections to community resources.

Specially trained Registered Nurses (RNs) partner with expecting mothers early in their pregnancy and continue personal home visits until the child’s second birthday. Ultimately, the program aims to empower first-time parents, promote healthy pregnancies, and foster optimal early childhood development.

organizations.description:
Address: 1002 SW D Ave. Phone: 580.250.1466 

 Teen Court, Inc. operates a highly successful juvenile delinquency prevention and diversion program for first-time, non-violent youth offenders. Serving as an alternative to the formal juvenile justice system, Teen Court utilizes a peer-driven courtroom model where local youth volunteers act as defense attorneys, prosecutors, bailiffs, and jurors under the supervision of adult judges. First-time offenders who have committed misdemeanor offenses (such as minor drug/alcohol violations, theft, or assault and battery) are sentenced by their peers to constructive sanctions, including community service, jury duty, and educational classes. By successfully completing their sentences, these youth avoid a formal juvenile record, while learning valuable lessons about accountability, anger management, and conflict resolution.

 This non-profit, low-cost neuter/spay facility has never turned away a pet owner regardless of his or her ability to pay. Vaccinations are on a walk-in basis 9am-4:30pm, Monday through Thursday. Surgeries are by appointment only.
